title: BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers)
body: An encoder-only Transformer pre-trained on unlabeled text with masked language modeling and next sentence prediction. Downstream tasks are handled by fine-tuning with one additional output layer.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: BERT model sizes: BERT_BASE vs BERT_LARGE
body: BERT_BASE has L=12 layers, H=768 hidden size, A=12 attention heads, and 110M total parameters. BERT_LARGE has L=24, H=1024, A=16, and 340M total parameters.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: Bidirectionality in BERT
body: Every layer of BERT conditions on both left and right context. Contrast: OpenAI GPT is a left-to-right Transformer, and ELMo concatenates independently trained left-to-right and right-to-left models.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: Why BERT does not use a standard language model objective
body: With bidirectional conditioning in a standard language model, each word could indirectly see itself. BERT therefore uses a masked language model objective instead of predicting the next word.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: Masked Language Model (MLM) pre-training
body: Select 15% of the WordPiece tokens in each sequence at random. Predict the original token at each selected position, using cross-entropy loss over the final hidden vector for that position.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: MLM 80/10/10 replacement rule
body: Of the 15% selected tokens: 80% of the time replace with [MASK], 10% of the time replace with a random token, and 10% of the time keep the original token unchanged.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: Why MLM does not always insert [MASK]
body: The [MASK] token never appears during fine-tuning. The random-token and unchanged-token cases in the 80/10/10 rule reduce the mismatch between pre-training and fine-tuning.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: Next Sentence Prediction (NSP)
body: A binarized sentence-pair task built from any monolingual corpus. For each example, 50% of the time B is the actual sentence that follows A (IsNext); 50% of the time B is a random sentence. The final [CLS] vector predicts the label.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: NSP ablation in the BERT paper
body: [REVIEW] The paper's 'No NSP' ablation trains BERT_BASE without next sentence prediction and reports a drop on some tasks. Exact per-task deltas were not checked against the table column layout; read Appendix C before relying on them.

title: BERT input format: [CLS], [SEP], and segment embeddings
body: The input begins with a special [CLS] token. Sentence pairs are separated by [SEP]. A learned segment embedding marks each token as sentence A or B. Each token's input vector sums its token, segment, and position embeddings.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: WordPiece tokenization in BERT
body: BERT uses WordPiece embeddings with a 30,000-token vocabulary. Words can split into subword pieces, marked with ## for continuation, e.g. 'playing' becomes 'play' + '##ing'.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: Tokenizer's role in the Hugging Face workflow
body: A tokenizer handles the first and last processing steps: it converts text into numerical inputs for the neural network, and converts model outputs back to text when needed.

title: Self-attention in BERT
body: Each BERT layer is a multi-head bidirectional self-attention stack, so every token attends to every other token in the sequence. The final hidden vector of [CLS] serves as the aggregate sequence representation.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: Fine-tuning: all parameters, one extra output layer
body: Start from pre-trained weights, add one task-specific output layer, and fine-tune all parameters on labeled data for the downstream task.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: Feature-based vs fine-tuning approach
body: A feature-based approach (e.g. ELMo) uses pre-trained representations as extra features for a task-specific model. BERT's fine-tuning approach updates all pre-trained parameters on the downstream task.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: BERT fine-tuning hyperparameter search
body: [REVIEW] The paper searches batch sizes of 16 or 32 and Adam learning rates of 5e-5, 3e-5, or 2e-5, for 2 to 4 epochs. GLUE fine-tuning used batch size 32 and 3 epochs. Ranges were read from a partial text extraction; verify against Appendix A.3.

title: BERT tasks: classification, token tagging, and span QA
body: Sentence-level outputs use the [CLS] vector, e.g. NLI and single-sentence classification. Token-level outputs use each token's final hidden vector, e.g. NER. Span QA predicts start and end positions over a passage.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: BERT results at publication
body: Reported: GLUE score 80.5 (7.7 point absolute improvement); MultiNLI accuracy 86.7% (4.6 point absolute improvement); SQuAD v1.1 test F1 93.2 (1.5 point); SQuAD v2.0 test F1 83.1 (5.1 point). Set new state-of-the-art on eleven NLP tasks.

metadata.source_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

title: BERT pre-training corpora
body: BooksCorpus (800M words) and English Wikipedia (2,500M words), using text passages only from Wikipedia.
